## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sikkhānisaṁsa Sutta* ("The Benefits of Training") is the 46th discourse of the *Itivuttaka* (found in the Dukanipāta at It 2.19, PTS p. 40) [SuttaCentral; Windisch 1889]. In this sutta, the Buddha instructs the mendicants to dwell having the training as their benefit (*sikkhānisaṁsā*), wisdom/discernment as supreme (*paññuttarā*), release as their essence (*vimuttisārā*), and mindfulness as their governing principle (*satādhipateyyā*) [Windisch 1889; SuttaCentral]. For those practicing in this manner, one of two fruits is to be expected: final knowledge in this very life (*diṭṭhe va dhamme aññā*) or, if there is a remainder of clinging, non-return (*anāgāmitā*) [Windisch 1889].
Full parallels are preserved in Chinese within the *Itivuttaka* translation (T 765.91) and the *Saṁyuktāgama* (SA 825) [SuttaCentral]. In addition, passage-level parallels to its verse material occur across several versions of the *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* traditions, including T 210.1, T 212.1, T 213.1, the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G3-Dhp 51–60), and the Sanskrit and Tibetan Udānavarga (UV 1 and Uv Kg 1) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus also records cross-language alignment with a section in the *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, the sutta shares notable formulas and textual reuse with adjacent *Itivuttaka* discourses such as the *Paṭisallāna Sutta* (Iti 45) and *Jāgariya Sutta* (Iti 47), as well as discourses in the *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46), the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 4 and AN 5), and the *Lakkhaṇa Sutta* (DN 30) [DharmaNexus].
